Smartbreadboard Programmable PCB

January – August 2026

1 / 4

I designed a programmable breadboard with 256 programmable crosspoints and developed Arduino firmware to control the connections. I tested addressing and control signals using logic analyser captures and schematic checks.

Objective: Reduce manual rewiring during electronics prototyping by allowing circuit connections to be selected and changed in software.

My role: PCB design, embedded firmware and signal verification. Individual research project.

My contribution: Designed a custom PCB in KiCad. Integrated two MT8816 switch matrices with an I2C GPIO expander. Developed Arduino firmware for connection control. Checked addressing and control signals using a logic analyser and schematic review.

Programmable connections: Two MT8816 switch matrices form the basis of the circuit-routing design, providing a total of 256 programmable crosspoints.

Firmware and interfaces: Arduino firmware controls circuit connections through a design incorporating an I2C GPIO expander.

Verification: Logic analyser captures and schematic checks were used to test addressing and control signals. This provides evidence about the control interface without implying comprehensive electrical characterisation.

Scope: Testing reported here covers addressing and control signals. Switch resistance, signal bandwidth, current limits and end-to-end circuit performance are not characterised on this page.
